decision.title: The QT4 driver: running tests, assertions, reports (packet )
decision.summary: sxml-qt4 run gives each test case its own processor under a 512 MiB budget allocator, evaluates assertions as XPath over $result, and reports pass, wrong-error, fail, error or not-run as text or JSON.

body.p: . sxml-qt4 run [--catalog] [--spec] [--test-set=NAME | TEST-LIST] [--format=text|json]; tests/qt4/driver/test_run.c, assertion.c, report.c, reason.c, command_run.c.

item.p: Isolation: each test case gets its own processor, made through a budget allocator (at most 512 MiB live; header-prefixed blocks) with maximum_evaluation_step_count 10^8; afterwards the budget must have no live allocation, else the outcome is error "leaked N allocations". A crash still ends the process: whole-suite runs use one process per test set. No --output=FILE: the CLI platform layer has no file writer (redirect standard output).

Environment: sources parsed with document and base URI = their uri (made absolute against the test-set file) or file:///SUITE-PATH; "." context value, "$name" variables item()*, uri available documents; params via select with as from sxml_xpath_parse_sequence_type; QName param names through the environment's namespaces; static base URI file:///SUITE-PATH of the test-set file unless given or #UNDEFINED. The resolver serves file:/// URIs as suite files and nothing else.

Assertions are XPath over $result (and $expected, the assertion's value) with the environment's namespaces: assert-eq = one atomic item and $result = $expected or deep-equal(...) (untyped cast, NaN = NaN); permutation by per-item deep-equal counts; assert-type = $result instance of TEXT; assert-xml = result written as XML (nodes by the adaptive serializer, atomics as escaped text joined by spaces), both sides parse-xmled in a wrapper element and deep-equal with comments and PIs (no full canonicalization; prefixes never matter); expected files lose their XML declaration and surrounding space. A wrong error code is the outcome "wrong-error" and counts as passed. Serialization assertions are "unsupported": the outcome is not-run, not fail (deviation from the task text). Verdicts combine worst-to-best fail < unsupported < wrong-error < pass on a fixed 32-frame stack ().

Outcomes: pass, wrong-error, fail, error (a status without an error record, a limit, a leak, an environment that cannot be set up), not-run (not applicable or unsupported). Text lists every non-pass, non-not-run case, a line per test set and a final total: line; JSON (schema in report.h) lists every case. Exit 1 on a fail or error.

Slice gate: ctest qt4/slice runs the slice and fails when fewer pass than tests/qt4/slice-baseline.txt (198); a higher count asks for the baseline to be raised. Goldens qt4/run_* over input/run-catalog.xml cover every assertion kind passing and failing.
